question: The European Union is facing a further increase in the cost of living as a result of the drawnout conflict in the Middle East and the Strait of Hormuz. Rising energy prices place a burden on households and businesses and are triggering a new wave of price hikes across Europe. According to Eurostat figures, annual inflation rose to 3.2 % in August 2026 in both the euro area and the European Union.

In the euro area, energy contributed 1.29 percentage points to the annual inflation rate. It is essential that immediate and decisive measures are taken to support households and businesses. There is an urgent need to reduce the excise duty on fuel, complete electricity interconnections, immediately trigger the special clause on electricity and fuel and reduce excise duty in EU Member States.
In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Will it reduce excise duty in EU Member States?
Will it look into the possibility of joint European action on electricity and fuels?
Will it cut this expenditure from national budgets?
